questions.stem:
Statements: Some files are lockers. All lockers are deposits. No deposits is a loans.
Conclusions:
I. Some files are deposits.
II. Some lockers are loans.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few files are lockers. All lockers are deposits. No deposits is a loans.
Conclusions:
I. Some files are not lockers.
II. No lockers is a loans.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few files are lockers. Some lockers are deposits. All deposits are loans.
Conclusions:
I. All files are loans.
II. No lockers is a loans.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: No files is a lockers. Some lockers are deposits. All deposits are loans.
Conclusions:
I. All files are loans.
II. Some loans are lockers.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:

Which conclusions follow? “Either” means at least one must hold, although neither is individually guaranteed.

questions.stem:
In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
access growth banking = mi ni vo
access rural digital = ka vo su
growth rural savings = ka mi ze
banking digital savings = ze ni su
access growth savings = ze mi vo
What is the code for “savings”?
questions.explanation: Answer: ze. Compare the intersections of the coded lines. The complete consistent mapping is: access = vo, growth = mi, banking = ni, rural = ka, digital = su, savings = ze.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 56 km east, turns right and walks 60 km, then turns right and walks 24 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 68. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 32 km along the initial direction and 60 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(32² + 60²) = 68 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 49 km north, turns right and walks 56 km, then turns right and walks 7 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 70. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 42 km along the initial direction and 56 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(42² + 56²) = 70 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 73 km east, turns left and walks 120 km, then turns left and walks 23 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 130. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 50 km along the initial direction and 120 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(50² + 120²) = 130 km.

questions.stem: G is the mother of C. A is the daughter of C. H is the father of C. How is A related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. H is a parent of C, and A is C’s daughter. Hence A is H’s grandchild.

questions.stem: A is the brother of B. B is the mother of F. D is the father of A and B. How is A related to F?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. A is the brother of F’s mother B. Therefore A is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: E is the only daughter of G. G is the father of E. H is the son of E. B is the sister of G. How is G related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. G is the father of E, and E is H’s mother. Thus G is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: In a queue of 52 candidates, a candidate is 21th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 29. New front rank = 21+3 = 24. Back rank = 52 − 24 + 1 = 29.

questions.stem: In a queue of 64 candidates, a candidate is 19th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 42. New front rank = 19+4 = 23. Back rank = 64 − 23 + 1 = 42.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹3000 each. One earns 20% profit and the other incurs 10% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 5833.33. Recover each cost separately: 3000×100/120 + 3000×100/90. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: Two inlet pipes can fill a tank in 38 and 57 hours. An outlet empties it in 76 hours. All three open together. Find the time (hours) to fill the empty tank. (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 32.57. Net rate = 1/38 + 1/57 − 1/76 = 7/228 tank/hour. Required time = 32.57 hours.

questions.stem: A boat covers 52 km in still water in 4 hours. If the stream flows at 4 km/h, how far (km) can it travel upstream in 2 hours?
questions.explanation: Answer: 18. Still-water speed = 13 km/h. Upstream speed = 13 − 4. Distance = speed × 2.

questions.stem: A and B invest in ratio 8:9. A invests for 12 months; B joins later and invests for 3 months. A receives ₹278400 profit. What is the total profit (₹)?
questions.explanation: Answer: 356700. Profit ratio is 96:27. Each ratio unit = ₹2900. Total = 123 × 2900.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹29000 earns ₹4350 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 31972.5. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 5%. Compound amount = 29000 × (1 + 5/100)².

questions.stem: A container holds 110 litres of pure milk. 22 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 70.4. Each replacement retains 4/5 of the milk. Remaining milk = 110 × (4/5)².

questions.stem: The average weight of 26 people is 50 kg. One person joins and the average rises by 1 kg. Find the new person’s weight (kg).
questions.explanation: Answer: 77. New total minus old total = (26+1)×(50+1) − 26×50 = 77.

questions.stem: A is twice as old as B. After 15 years their ages will be in ratio 3:2. What is the present sum of their ages?
questions.explanation: Answer: 45. Let B = x, A = 2x. (2x+15)/(x+15) = 3/2 gives x = 15. Present sum = 3x.

questions.stem: A 280 m train moving at 82.8 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 7.2 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 13.33. Relative speed = (82.8 − 7.2) ×5/18 = 21 m/s. Time = 280/21.

questions.stem: The price of a commodity increases by 50%. A household keeps spending fixed at ₹2800. By what percentage must consumption decrease? (Round to two decimals.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 33.33. New quantity / old quantity = 100/150. Reduction percentage = 50/150 ×100.
